summary: NCBI Taxonomy provides curated classification and nomenclature for organisms represented in public sequence databases. Preserve taxon identifiers and species context, and distinguish database curation from the broader scientific literature.

NCBI Gene integrates gene records across many species with nomenclature, reference sequences, maps, pathways, variations, phenotypes and links to related resources. Preserve organism context and evidence provenance.

WHO-FIC includes ICD, ICF and ICHI as global health classification standards. Attach classification release/version, language, jurisdiction and date; classifications support interoperability and statistics but do not replace clinical judgment.

Health infrastructure can be modeled using facility types and population-normalized measures such as hospitals, health posts, health centres, district/rural hospitals, provincial hospitals and specialized hospitals per 100,000 population. Preserve provider type and source methodology when available.

A health-system ontology should cover service delivery, health workforce, health information systems, medical products/vaccines/technologies, financing, and leadership/governance. Use versioned, source-attributed indicators for comparisons.

Population-level health statistics are not individual diagnoses. Personal health information requires explicit authorization and privacy controls; public-health indicators and biological associations must not be converted into unsupported individual medical conclusions.
